subject: Renewal & capacity upgrade: 16→32 GPUs — proposal and SLA
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acuitylabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contract renewal: proposal for increased reserved capacity

Hi Jordan,

Hope youre well. Our annual renewal for the Redwood Dedicated pool is coming up (current term ends 2027-05-31) and the usage profile over the last 6 months shows consistent saturation of our 16-GPU pool. We ran additional stress tests attached and concluded we need to move to 32 reserved GPUs to meet latency SLOs during peak windows.

High-level asks:
- Upgrade reserved capacity from 16 -> 32 GPUs starting at renewal date.
- Updated per-hour reserved pricing and total monthly committed cost for 12- and 24-month terms.
- Throughput guarantee for our primary model (approx 1.2k tokens/sec sustained across the pool) or an agreed fallback model with predictable performance.
- Clear rollback/fallback policy in case performance regressions occur post-migration.

Can you share a preliminary commercial proposal and any technical caveats? Wed like to present numbers to procurement by April 22.

Attached: Acuity_MAAP_Throughput_SLA.pdf, acq_load_test_results.zip

Thanks,
Maria Garcia
Head of Platform Engineering
Acuity Labs

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract renewal: proposal for increased reserved capacity (technical note)

Jordan / Grace,

Reviewing Acuity's load tests: the model config shows long context windows (~2k tokens) and KV cache hit rates in the 82-88% range. A 32-GPU reserved pool gives us headroom, but sustained 1.2k tokens/sec across the pool assumes aggressive batching and no heavy single-request tails. Operational caveats:

- For guaranteed sustained throughput we must set a per-request max length or accept degraded latency for the rare oversized requests.
- Recommend enabling KV prefix caching + adaptive batching; this reduces effective token throughput requirement by ~20% in our tests.
- If Acuity needs strict per-second guarantees, we should add a "throughput buffer" of 15% and an SLA clause that allows for short daily rate-limited queues during maintenance windows.

Commercially, we can recommend two pricing constructs:
1) 12-month term: $4.95 per GPU-hour reserved (32 GPU pool) — standard support, 99.9% uptime SLA, throughput buffer included in the commitment calculation.
2) 24-month term: $4.45 per GPU-hour reserved (32 GPU pool) — includes one planned maintenance buffer and 24/7 priority support.

Both options require an explicit rollback plan (snapshot + traffic cutover) and a canary rollout window. Docs attached for the rollback/runbook template.

- Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_amendment_16to32_redwood.docx

Date: 2027-04-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 16->32 GPU reserved pool amendment (commercial + SLA)

Maria,

Thanks again for the patience while we validated the operational side. Attached is our formal proposal and a redlineable amendment. Summary below:

Scope: upgrade Redwood Dedicated reserved pool from 16 -> 32 GPUs, effective 2027-06-01.
Term options and per-GPU reserved pricing (all numbers USD):
- 12-month commitment: $4.95 per GPU-hour reserved. Estimated monthly invoice (32 GPUs x 24h x 30d): $114,048/month.
- 24-month commitment: $4.45 per GPU-hour reserved. Estimated monthly invoice (32 GPUs x 24h x 30d): $102,432/month.

SLA & operational items:
- Throughput target: baseline 1,200 tokens/sec sustained across the pool for the primary model family, subject to request-size gating (max 2,048 tokens/request) and KV caching enabled.
- Performance buffer: Redwood commits a 15% capacity buffer to be accounted for in surge periods; exceptions allowed for emergency maintenance with advance notice.
- Canary rollout: 2-week canary with 10% traffic then 50% then full (rollback plan included).
- Credits: partial-month credit if sustained >5% SLA miss in a billing month.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm preferred term (12m vs 24m) and any procurement POs needed.
2) We will issue a formal amendment PDF and DocuSign envelope within 48 hours once you confirm.
3) Ops and Eng will schedule a technical kickoff to finalize canary windows and cutover plan.

Attachments: proposed_amendment_16to32_redwood.docx (redlineable), Acuity_MAAP_Throughput_SLA.pdf

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Add a quarterly maintenance calendar stub with proposed weeks so we can align internal change freezes.

If you can incorporate those two items in the redline, procurement will sign the 24-month amendment and send the PO. Please send the DocuSign when ready; well have final sign-off by EOD April 29 if everything aligns.
